claims.claim_text: To legitimately represent the working class, a mass working-class party that contests elections and builds movements must be born out of a level of class struggle and unity far greater than exists today.
Until class struggle and unity can support a mass working-class party, Bread and Roses sees DSA as a pre-party organization, one of many groups developing the forces necessary to build that party.

An oppositional electoral strategy independent from the Democratic Party apparatus must reject the idea that socialists can capture the Democratic Party and instead seek to break unions and social movements from their dependence on the Democratic Party establishment.

Campaigns by class-struggle candidates who are not socialists but advance key parts of the platform can help build class consciousness and polarize and eventually split the Democratic Party coalition.
